comments.text_zh: 作为一个外行，我不清楚这些 malacidins 是否是在菌丝体（真菌）中发现的。我倾向于认为很可能是。如果是这样，在泥土里发现它们其实并不令人意外（30% 的泥土由菌丝体构成——包括活的和死的）。这似乎是寻找新抗生素的显而易见之处。对任何对真菌感兴趣的人，我极力推荐去听 Paul Stamets 谈这个主题。和 HN 上的很多人一样，我吸收大量信息，而他最近接受 Joe Rogan 的访谈[0]是我多年来遇到的最引人入胜的东西之一。[0] [VIDEO]
comments.text: As a lay person, it's not clear to me whether these malacidins were found in mycelium (fungi). I'm inclined to think this is likely. If so, finding them in dirt is not really surprising (30% of dirt is comprised of mycelium - living and dead). It seems like the obvious place to look for new antibiotics. For anyone that's interested in fungi I can't recommend listening to Paul Stamets talk on the subject more highly. Like a lot of people here on HN I take in a lot of information and his recent interview with Joe Rogan[0] was one of the most fascinating things I've come across in years. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我学的是工程/物理，过去一年因为产生了兴趣而涉足了农业领域，也观察了当地一家有机农场的运作。这其实相当迷人。我目前正在上 Dr. Elaine Ingham 创建的课程，她是一位研究土壤生物学的微生物学家，做过一些非常了不起的研究。她还曾在 Colorado State University 工作过，这绝不可能是巧合！下面是实际发生情况的内情，因为我们在农业中几百年来一直把这件事搞错了。养分（N、Ph、Mg、K 等）被结合在土壤中的物质上，这些物质从岩石到卵石，再到砂、粉砂和黏土不等。我们一直在通过翻耕做法和大型机械破坏土壤，这些做法和机械造成压实层，导致厌氧条件，使土壤中“好的”生物学死亡，也阻止根系长到它们需要的深度。结果发现，养分变得可被植物根系利用的方式，是细菌/真菌打破它们与前述物质（岩石等）的结合，然后，更有趣的是，它们被更高营养级的捕食者吃掉，而这些捕食者把养分以植物可利用的形式拉出来！一些有趣的事实：- 根系向土壤中释放糖类（光合产物），这会根据其对养分的需求以及 pH 要求吸引特定的细菌/真菌（细菌释放提高 pH 的物质，真菌释放酸来降低
comments.text: I studied engineering/physics and I've dipped into the agricultural field the past year having developed an interest in it, also observing the operations of a local organic farm. It's actually quite fascinating. I'm currently following a course created by Dr. Elaine Ingham, who is a microbiologist that studies soil biology and has done some really amazing research. She also worked at Colorado State University, which can't be a coincidence! Here's the lowdown of what happens, because we've been getting this wrong for centuries in agriculture. The nutrients (N, Ph, Mg, K, etc) are bound to materials in the soil ranging from rocks to pebbles, to sands, silts and clays. We have been destroying the soil by tilling practices and large machinery which are creating compaction layers that lead to anaerobic conditions causing the "good" biology in the soil to die and also preventing roots from growing to the depth they need. It turns out that the way that the nutrients become available to the roots of the plant is by means of the bacteria/fungi breaking their bonds from the previously mentioned materials (rocks, etc) and then, even more interestingly, they get eaten by higher trophic level predators who shit out the nutrients in plant available form!
